root_cause.text: In the Apple Silicon SMC hwmon driver (`drivers/hwmon/macsmc-hwmon.c`), the voltage sensor population path incorrectly used the temperature sensor array and a mismatched node prefix, causing sensor entries to be written into the wrong `hwmon` subarray and leading to out-of-bounds access/data corruption when both sensor types were present.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `for_each_child_of_node_with_prefix(hwmon_node, key_node, "volt-")` to `"voltage-"` and switches `sensor = &hwmon->temp.sensors[hwmon->temp.count];` to `sensor = &hwmon->volt.sensors[hwmon->volt.count];`, and the CVE description explicitly says this bug could cause “out-of-bounds memory access or data corruption when both temperature and voltage sensors were present.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the f32 SMC encoding logic to derive sign and normalized mantissa/exponent values correctly before writing them to hardware.
intent_record.what: In macsmc_hwmon_write_f32(), the code changes how the sign and floating-point exponent/mantissa are computed: `exp` is no longer initialized to 0 at declaration, `neg` is now derived from `value < 0` instead of comparing `abs(value)` to `value`, the normalized bit position is stored directly in `exp = __fls(val)`, the mantissa-shift logic is simplified to shift `val` by `exp - 23` or `23 - exp`, and the mantissa field is now masked with `FLT_MANT_MASK` when assembling `fval`.
intent_record.how: This alters the runtime encoding of integer input into the SMC's custom f32 format so that the sign is determined directly from the original value and the mantissa is constrained to the field width after normalization. It prevents incorrect sign detection and reduces the chance of writing improperly formed floating-point bit patterns to the hardware.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix voltage sensor enumeration to use the correct node prefix and sensor array.
intent_record.what: In macsmc_hwmon_populate_sensors(), the child-node prefix used for voltage sensors was changed from "volt-" to "voltage-", and the target sensor array indexing was changed from hwmon->temp.sensors[hwmon->temp.count] to hwmon->volt.sensors[hwmon->volt.count].
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code now iterates over device tree child nodes named with the "voltage-" prefix and stores created sensors into the voltage sensor list instead of incorrectly using the temperature sensor array. This fixes voltage sensor population so those sensors are registered in the right place.
